question: What is the projected annual growth rate of India-UK bilateral trade under the new Free Trade Agreement (FTA)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.15**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The projected annual growth rate of India-UK bilateral trade under the new Free Trade Agreement (FTA) is estimated to be **0.15 (15%)**, showcasing significant economic potential.
 
• The India-UK FTA aims to enhance trade and investment ties, reducing tariffs and boosting market access for goods and services.
 
• India is the UK’s second-largest source of investment, and the FTA is expected to further strengthen this relationship.
 
• Both countries are focusing on sectors like **pharmaceuticals, technology, automotive, textiles, and financial services** for mutual benefits.
 
• The agreement aligns with the UK’s post-Brexit strategy to forge stronger trade partnerships outside the European Union.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Free Trade Agreement (FTA):**

 
 
• An FTA is a pact between two or more nations to reduce barriers to imports and exports, such as tariffs, quotas, and restrictions.
 
• FTAs facilitate increased trade and economic integration between the participating countries.
 
• They often include provisions for intellectual property rights, labor standards, and environmental protection.
 
 
 
• **India-UK Trade Relationship:**
 
 
• The UK is one of India’s largest trade partners, with bilateral trade amounting to billions annually.
 
• Key exports from India include textiles, pharmaceuticals, software, and automotive components.
 
• The UK exports machinery, chemicals, and financial services to India.
 
 
 
• **Post-Brexit Opportunities:**
 
 
• The UK is prioritizing FTAs with non-EU countries to diversify its trade portfolio post-Brexit.
 
• India offers a large and growing market for UK businesses, particularly in sectors like technology and healthcare.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:**
 
 
• The FTA is expected to create jobs, increase investments, and enhance consumer choice in both countries.
 
• Strategic sectors like renewable energy and infrastructure development stand to benefit significantly.
